rule: Not calls: passing a method reference (`x::m`, `self.m` without call), enum-variant/data construction (Rust `Some(x)`, `E::V(..)`, Haskell `Con {..}`), casts, language constructs (`isset`, `empty`, `sizeof`), declarations/function heads, module attributes, typespecs, field access without a call. | **Body-less member declarations of scanned types are defined in the scan (high)**: a call that resolves to a method declared without a body by a trait, interface, protocol, abstract class or pure-virtual C++ declaration (`fn now() -> u64;`, `virtual void OnError() = 0;`, `def m: Int`, an interface method) is high when that declaring type is in the scan, exactly as Go interface calls are. | Typed receivers (decision A, all statically typed languages and typed PHP/Groovy declarations): a receiver whose type is given by a declaration — local, parameter, field/property (including `$var->prop` / `obj.field` chains whose property has a declared type), catch parameter, for-loop variable, pattern binding — or by `= new T(...)` gives `T#m` (high if defined in the scan, else medium). | Import statements are not calls.
notes: Only two calls: `sh!.area()` and `sh2.area()`, both on locals declared `: Shape` -> `types.Shape#area` (interface method of a scanned type, high).
